commands_raw:
In [color=green][b]Genome Garden[/b][/color] all living things are defined by genes makeup that defines everything about them, just like in real life.
---
We've given these genes are given names based on the primary effects they have on the plant e.g. [b]colour_1[/b] or [b]pigment[/b].
---
In the case of the [b]colour_1[/b] gene we've discovered the [color=RED][b]R[/b][/color] allele which appears to be responsible for creating a red color!"
---
In each flower, each gene is made up of two alleles. This tulip for example has two [color=RED][b]R[/b][/color] alleles for it's [b]colour_1[/b] gene. Hover over it to take a look!
signal(show_flower,red_tulip)
name: Tutorial_start

commands_raw:
signal(skip_text_animation)
In each flower, each gene is made up of two alleles. This tulip for example has two [color=RED][code]R[/code][/color] alleles for it's [code]colour_1[/code] gene. Hover over it to take a look!
---
signal(show_flower,yellow_tulip)
When we cross-breed flowers together the child inherits one allele from each parent for each gene. Here's another tulip with [color=GOLD][code]Y[/code][/color] alleles for the [u]colour_1[/u] gene. The [color=GOLD][code]Y[/code][/color] allele is responsible or producing a [color=GOLD]yellow[/color] colour! Take a look at the Yellow flower
name: on_red_tulip_hover

commands_raw:
signal(skip_text_animation)
When we cross-breed flowers together the child inherits one allele from each parent for each gene. Here's another tulip with [color=GOLD][code]Y[/code][/color] alleles for the [u]colour_1[/u] gene. The [color=GOLD][code]Y[/code][/color] allele is responsible or producing a [color=GOLD]yellow[/color] colour! Take a look at the Yellow flower
---
signal(show_breeder)
signal(set_state_step,breeding_orange)
When we cross-breed two flowers together each child inherits one allele from each parent for each gene. Let's try breeding them together and see what happens!
name: on_yellow_tulip_hover

commands_raw:
Woah! An [color=orange]Orange[/color] flower. Different alleles can interact with each other in different ways. The [color=red]R[/color] allele and [color=gold]Y[/color] allele in this case are said to be [i]Codominant[/i] meaning that both alleles can be expressed at the same time, or that neither one is dominant over the other. 
---
signal(set_state_step,breeding_rb)
signal(show_flower,blue_tulip)
signal(hide_flower,yellow_tulip)
Here's another flower from our nursery. This one has two coppies of the [color=royal_blue]b[/color] allele. We've had some interesting results breeding this one. Why don't you try cross breeding it with the red flower.
name: on_orange_flower_bred

commands_raw: Huh. Looks like were only getting red children? Let me take a closer look at them. Interesting! They are all getting a `R` from the red flower and a `b` from the blue, that is they have `colour_1: Rb`. Looks like the red allele's effect is dominant over the blue.
name: on_third_rb_flower

commands_raw: Nice try but we're trying to breed a Red flower with a Yellow flower at the moment. Try right clicking to up-root one of the parents and re-plant the space with the other colour.
name: on_same_parent_orange_breed

commands_raw: Nice try but we're trying to breed a [color=Red]Red[/color] flower with a [color=Blue]Blue[/color] flower at the moment. Try right clicking to up-root one of the parents and re-plant the space with the other colour.
name: on_same_parent_rb_breed
